propositions: On the agentic execution path, tool-result message history is re-sent uncached every turn, causing input cost to grow quadratically in the number of turns rather than being cached after the first occurrence.

The cache_settings_for function configures only two of four available cache breakpoints (anthropic_cache_instructions and anthropic_cache_tool_definitions), omitting the message-tail caching knobs needed for multi-turn agents.
Cost savings from uncached re-transmission are invisible to rebar's telemetry because the system-block cache hit causes warn_if_cache_ineffective to never fire despite massive wasteful re-sends.

Anthropic and Bedrock have asymmetric cache control APIs: Anthropic accepts a top-level anthropic_cache key while Bedrock rejects it and requires bedrock_cache_messages instead, requiring provider-specific configuration logic.
